title: Massachusetts's 5th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Massachusetts's 5th Congressional District features incumbent Democratic House Minority Whip Katherine Clark facing primary challenges from the left by Jonathan Paz and Tarik Samman, with independent candidate Derek Fleming also in the race. The district, which covers parts of Middlesex, Norfolk, and Suffolk counties including Cambridge, Framingham, and Waltham, has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+24 and has been held by Democrats since 1975. No Republican candidates filed to run in the primary according to the Massachusetts Secretary of State. The Democratic primary is scheduled for September 1, 2026.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of mid-2026. The district is considered safely Democratic by major election forecasters.

candidates.name: Katherine Clark
candidates.summary: Katherine Clark has represented Massachusetts's 5th Congressional District since winning a special election in 2013. She serves as House Minority Whip, the second-highest ranking Democrat in the U.S. House, and is a member of the House Appropriations Committee. Clark has made the opioid crisis, clean energy, and climate change key legislative priorities and has raised nearly $2 million for her 2026 re-election campaign.

candidates.name: Jonathan Paz
candidates.summary: Jonathan Paz is a former Waltham city councilor who announced a primary challenge to incumbent Katherine Clark in 2026. Born in Boston and having spent eight years growing up in Bolivia, Paz served four years on the Waltham City Council before an unsuccessful mayoral run in 2023. He founded the Fuerza Community Defense Network to monitor ICE activity and advocates for abolishing ICE, redirecting funds to housing, healthcare, and education.

candidates.name: Tarik Samman
candidates.summary: Tarik Samman is a 27-year-old Harvard Law School researcher challenging incumbent Katherine Clark from the left in the 2026 Democratic primary. Born in Lowell to a Syrian immigrant family, Samman spent much of his childhood in Damascus after his family left the U.S. following the 9/11 attacks before returning in 2014. He advocates for greater investments in housing, healthcare, and childcare, and pledges to oppose weapons transfers to Israel and support recognition of a Palestinian state.

candidates.name: Derek Fleming
candidates.summary: Derek Fleming is an independent candidate and small business owner from Arlington running for Massachusetts's 5th Congressional District. Ballotpedia lists him as a general election candidate running on a structural reform platform. Fleming's campaign emphasizes changing how Congress operates and addressing systemic issues in government.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race, which moderates confidence. However, the structural fundamentals overwhelmingly favor a Democratic hold: MA-05 has a Cook PVI of D+24, has been held by Democrats since 1975, and no Republican candidate filed to run. Incumbent Katherine Clark is House Minority Whip (the second-ranking House Democrat) and has raised nearly $2 million for her re-election, far outpacing her primary challengers. Her two Democratic primary opponents (Jonathan Paz, a former Waltham city councilor, and Tarik Samman, a 27-year-old Harvard researcher) are lower-profile challengers running from the left. The general election independent candidate (Derek Fleming) faces steep odds in a D+24 district against the Democratic nominee. While the September 1 Democratic primary introduces some nominal uncertainty, Clark is the prohibitive favorite. The Democratic nominee will be an overwhelming favorite in the general election, making this a safe Democratic seat.
